Kimberly / Ben — quick finance read below.

1) Invoice routing: We can bill the invoice to BrightCloud Holdings Ltd (UK) if the billing address on the Order Form uses the UK legal name and VAT/tax registration field is captured as "N/A" for non-EU customers. However, bank remittance can point to our US collection account; the invoice PDF will show billing to the UK entity and payment instructions to Redwood (US). (We do this often for multi-entity customers.)

2) Tax evidence: For US payments we require: either a W-9 (if BrightCloud payer is US) or a certificate of tax residency (if claiming treaty benefits). Since the payer is US, W-9 + EIN should be sufficient for our records. If BrightCloud insists the UK entity be billed, we need the UK entity's tax registration number for their records (they may supply a VAT registration or confirm non-EU status).

3) Clawback / reconciliation: quarterly reconciliation is workable but increases bookkeeping overhead. Proposed compromise: quarterly reconciliation with a 90-day settlement window and an annual cap equal to 10% of the committed spend for the contract year. Language suggestion: "Customer may reconcile actual usage vs committed units quarterly; any overpayment eligible for credit will be applied within 90 days, subject to an annual cap of 10% of committed spend."

I've attached an example invoice PDF and a short note that legal can use to craft the precise Order Form clause. If legal prefers 6 months, I'd accept that too but prefer quarterly for faster customer-facing resolution.

Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
